page.layout: One page of running text, single column. Page number at the head, centred. Heading "De Dipthongis." centred above the second block. Catchword at lower right below the last line. No running head, no margin notes.

main_text.p: 1 In medio dictionis post vocalem brevem nisi sit sub litera daghessata.
Apud Chaldæos Scheva simplex quiescit etiam post vocalem longam quamcunque, ut [illegible, ~6 letters] petitio Dan. 4. 14.
Omnibus literis Scheva convenit, at cum א & ה rarissime reperitur.
Gutturales nunquam admittunt Scheva vocale, sed solum mutum, at Scheva compositum est ipsorum proprium.
main_text.head: De Dipthongis.
main_text.p: ו & י post Camets, Tsere, Pathach & Chirec in sine dictionis, cum vocalibus hisce dipthongos constituunt, ו triplicem facit dipthongum, viz. 1. (au) per ּ, ut [illegible, ~3 letters] mansuetus, sæpe interveniente ו ut [illegible, ~3 letters] vel per , ut [illegible, ~3 letters] regula. 2. (eu) ut [illegible, ~4 letters] pacificus. 3. (iu) ut [illegible, ~3 letters] os ejus.

ו etiam triplicem facit ai, oi, et ui, ut [illegible, ~3 letters] panai, [illegible, ~2 letters] goi, [illegible, ~3 letters] galui, Judæi vero dipthongum in ו non agnoscunt, sed ו ut consonam pronunciant, & de ו dubitatur à quibusdam. Irregulare est [illegible, ~5 letters] Jer 26. 18. quod legendum & pronunciandum [illegible, ~5 letters] Jerushalajim. Apud Chaldæos fit (eu) dipthongus ex ו tum in fine ut apud Hebræos, tum in medio, ut [illegible, ~4 letters] bestia, ubi & ו intervenit.
Jod facit (ai) dipthongum apud Chaldæos, per ו ante ' in medio ut [illegible, ~4 letters] prima. Dan.7.4.

page.notes: Hebrew and Aramaic words are printed with vowel points; I could not read them letter by letter, so each is marked illegible with an approximate letter count. Mixed-up Hebrew letters in the rules (ו, י, א, ה) are read from the scan but not verified against the points. The Hebrew word for "petitio" and the Hebrew letters near "ut" in the dipthong examples are the least certain. Printed "Jer 26. 18." and "Dan.7.4." are copied as printed. The running head is absent, and the text on this page is a continuous block with no margin notes.
